sources.says: AAC 1971 report: Cockscomb/Park Glacier headwall variation, snow-and-ice ramp ~60 deg at top crossing the schrund (historical, no pitch count)

Neighbouring Baker ice headwalls are pitched technical ice (2-4 pitches, screws); stored text itself says sustained ice pitches ~50 m. Park Glacier Headwall has no modern route page, so grade AI3 is the app's stored ice_grade
6 pitches, Grade IV; couloir steepens to a short ~80 degree step; second shorter step of rock or ice above
At the constriction there may be 20-30 m of exposed ice; a solid belay is advisable when roped
Triple Couloirs WI3 M3 steep snow; steep snow/ice pitches (runnels) separate the couloirs
Three long snow couloirs separated by two ice runnels (first runnel three pitches, second one pitch); stored note itself says plan to belay
Moderate to steep snow, direct line may hold AI2+ ice; pickets and/or ice screws; a party used a running belay of 2 screws and 2 pickets
Reports of first ~3 pitches fairly easy with short steep ice under 15 ft; route took pickets and screws (running belay, so borderline vs simul)
Party did running belays on pickets/screws on the Mowich face, then as it became too steep and icy switched to standard belays; 40-55 deg grade IV ice
Central Mowich Face IV AI2 60 degrees, pickets and a couple screws
Ice roughly AI2-AI3 with steep snow and route-finding; lower glacier is a long weave up steep snow/ice between seracs and crevasses, not a single pitch; crux is the bergschrund band near 7,800 ft
2009 report: bergschrunds are the crux (Section 2 correctly stays a pitch)

routes.pitches_sources: Couloir is 35-45 deg snow; the 5.6 exit chimney is simul-climbed with gear by many parties (SummitPost log 2013). Stored 3 not verified.
routes.notes: No change. Exit pitch correctly a pitch.

routes.pitches_sources: Mountaineers: Grade II snow/ice, 4 screws + 3 pickets per team, upper rock cliffs force several pitches left. No source gives a pitch count.
routes.notes: Single entry labelled '1-13 (roped/simul-climbed sections)' is drawn as a leg. Sources do not settle pitched vs simul; left unchanged (grade AI2 vs AI3 also disagrees: Lemke says AI3).

routes.pitches_sources: No source found online; entry 0 covers 1-3 pitches (3 per the stored note).
MP lists 20 pitches (WI3 M3, Grade IV); guide/trip reports say most parties pitch only 3-4 and simul the rest; runnels are ~3 pitches, second runnel 1 pitch.
routes.notes: The Runnels entry (one entry, ~3 pitches) is correct as pitch. Couloirs correctly legs.

routes.pitches_sources: Stored notes: P1 crux, central flow two long pitches, final icy gully a rope-length. Online pages (AAC 2015, CascadeClimbers 2015) only partly readable.
routes.notes: See unsure: ice curtain and glacier step, upper snowfields.

routes.pitches_sources: No authoritative pitch count; MP grade II, one report says first ~3 pitches fairly easy.
Entry 1 is 'x3' (three ~50 m pitches) so counts as 3 pitches if the drawer expands it; no modern source found for the count.
routes.notes: Drawer counts entries, not the x3, so 1 vs stored 4 may need handling.

routes.pitches_sources: SummitPost: 4000 ft of 40-55 deg ice done with running belays on pickets and occasional screws.
routes.notes: Running belay = travel; no change. Rock band 'grade: 5th class' does not match the 5.x regex so draws as a leg although it is roped rock; see unsure.

routes.pitches_sources: Ski and climb reports: 45-50 deg sustained slope climbed (even skied); bergschrund crossing is a short step belayed only if marginal.
routes.notes: No change; all entries correctly legs.

routes.pitches_sources: Upper face: 4-6 pitches of 50-60 deg snow on harder variation (stored note); lower face is running belay on pickets.
Mountaineers and 2018 conditions report: 55-60 deg snow with ice a few inches down takes screws; no pitch count.
routes.notes: Upper Mowich Face traverse left as leg (unsure).

routes.pitches_sources: No source found for route; Section 3 rock 5.3-5.6 correctly a pitch.
routes.notes: Section 2 'Ice to 65°' mixes roped glacier travel and ice steps; unsure.

routes.pitches_sources: No pitch count found; MP Grade IV, AI2-3.
routes.notes: After change only the schrund band (Section 2) is a pitch.

routes.pitches_sources: MP: 6 pitches, 1700 ft. A 2011 CascadeClimbers poster counted 12-15 shorter/simul pitches; 2010 report used a 30 m rope for 6 pitches.
routes.notes: Ridge 1-4 entries (grade 'low 5th' / 'mid 5th') do NOT match the pitch regex (only 'easy/low 5th' does) and draw as legs though they are roped rock; with them the count reaches ~6 as stored. Needs a 5.x token (e.g. '5.4, low 5th') - not an ice question, so left to caller.

routes.pitches_sources: MP: 12 pitches, Grade III, continuous ice for almost the entire face, start has several WI2-3 pitches up a 600 ft ramp.
routes.notes: Only 2 entries drawn as pitches vs 12 stored; entries 2 and 3 (snowfields, labelled as pitch numbers) are probably pitched but sources do not say; see unsure.

unsure.why: Second step 'short rock or ice'; pitons used for belays in one report, but no grade; likely pitched, left.
Ridge 1-3 and 4-6 (low/mid 5th) are roped rock, currently drawn as legs because grade text lacks 5.x token; rock, outside ice scope.
Vertical ice curtain is clearly pitched (stored note: good protection) but no source gave a grade.
Snow to 70 deg, pickets and screws running protection; pitched vs simul not settled.
Roped vs simul not settled; grade AI2 vs AI3 disputed.
Hourglass entry rock/ice ~40-50 ft likely a roped step; no source.
Rock band 5th class is roped rock; grade lacks 5.x.
55-60 deg face traverse, front-pointing with screws in ice; running belay vs pitches unsettled.
Ice to 65 deg mixes glacier travel with steps; no source found.
Snowfields labelled as pitch numbers 2 and 3 on a 12-pitch route; sources do not say whether belayed.
